## Notes

I want to investigate whether PHS can stratify individuals by prostate cancer diagnosis, risk of mortality within 5 years of first diagnosis, and metastatic disease (based on pharmaceutical registry). I would also like to know to what extent my study populations represent the larger population in Norway and in Rogaland. These are somewhat different populations because Rogaland is a random sample whereas the Heritable Cancer cohort is recruited based on self-reported family incidence of cancer. Therefore, the HC cohort likely has a higher rate of cancer than the general population whereas HUSK should be representative.

What do I need to do to finish this paper and submit it?

-   A question: Does a PCa PHS developed in another population effectively stratify PCa risk in an unobserved sample population (Norwegian)?

-   Will this generalize to the whole population, not just the weird cohort that we have?

-   Prospect cohort could include undiagnosed PCA, how does performance compare in a case-only analysis?

-   How do rare variants compete with common variants/genetic risk scores for risk stratification?

## Research Questions

-   validate that the 601 score (preprint Vassy et al.) works and that it is better than the 290 (Huynh-Le 2022) These are clinically interesting because they are being tested in a prospective clinical trial (5000 person study) <https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05926102>
-   try to PCARE model of family history, PCA of ancestry (nordic specific PCA?)
-   second preprint: focus on specificity: Age at metastasis high PGS increased risk of metastic disease (Dornisch et al.)
-   If you have a high genetic score, are you more likely have a rare variant?
-   Does the performance I get worse if I remove those with rare variants?
-   How important is it that I haven't done WGS?
-   Do you get the most bang for your buck from genotyping?
-   If you have the PGS, do rare variants matter?
-   What is the added value of WGS?
-   How much can we stratify with prediction in the general population? plug in the prostate cancer rate for the general pop from kreftregisteret then straify by PHS score
-   Stratify by risk of death (PCa death or all-cause mortality?) within 5 years of diagnosis
-   Limitation of registry data is that if they don't have a diagnosis, it is possible controls include undiagnoses prostate cancer. Do a case-only analysis in HUSK.
-   check prescription registry to see if PCa diagnoses got certain treatments, length of treatment, hormone therapy long-term
